records.performance_summary: Validation on sequestered U.S. data (239 patients acquired over two months at one U.S. site with the predicate device; ground truth from three licensed sonographers). Auto Plane Detection (50 patients, age 20-98, BMI 16.4-71.6, EF severity strata balanced): acceptance criterion >90% agreement with sonographer-selected views for each of A4C/A3C/A2C/SAX; achieved for all four views with an average pass rate of 97%; subgroup logistic regression showed no confounders. Quick Strain (50 patients): 68% average reduction in operation time, all ICC(2,1) >0.75, NRMSE for EDV/ESV/EF/GLS <10% vs conventional 2D WMT LV. Auto LVOT (45 patients): 78% average reduction in operation time over 3 heart cycles, ICC >0.75, NRMSE <10% vs manual LVOT trace. Auto AoV (45 patients): 71% average reduction in operation time, ICC >0.75, NRMSE <10% vs manual AV trace. Quote (p.8): "Auto Plane Detection achieved these criteria for each of the four views, with an average pass rate of 97% across these four views." Quote (p.9): "All prespecified performance criteria were passed by Quick Strain which achieved an average 68% reduction in operation time". Quote (p.10): "Auto LVOT demonstrated an average 78% reduction in operation time (3 consecutive heart cycles)". Quote (p.11): "demonstration by Auto AoV of an average 71% reduction in operation time (3 consecutive heart cycles)".

records.exclusion_reason: The only AI/ML feature named is 3rd Harmonic Imaging (3-HI), a deep-learning abdominal image-quality filter validated on abdominal images from 30 U.S. patients by three radiologists (p.8-9). Other changes (SMI Angio Mode, Precision+ Fine Processing, Auto Tune for SWE/SWD, Windows 11) are non-AI and non-cardiac. No cardiac AI feature is named in this summary; previously cleared cardiac AI (Auto EF / 2D WMT Full-assist, Auto Plane Detection, etc.) is presumably carried over from predicate K242808 but is not mentioned.

records.performance_summary: No numeric results reported. Both AI/ML features were integrated without modification from reference device K223017 and re-tested on a representative subset of the original clinical validation data using the same acceptance criteria and same ground truth; all passed. Quote (p.7): "In this submission, 2D Wall Motion Tracking with Full-assist function for left ventricle (LV) and Auto EF with Full-assist function for LV, as cleared with the reference device, were both integrated without modification into UltraExtend NX, V2.0." Quote (p.8): "The results of this testing demonstrate that both features perform as intended when integrated into the subject device, and with substantial equivalence as with the reference device."

notes: All six summaries read in full (letter pages, IFU pages, 510(k) summary) plus a regex keyword sweep for AI/ML/deep learning/auto/algorithm terms. Three clearances are cardiac AI: K212333 (first FDA text to label Canon's 2D WMT Full-assist and Auto EF Full-assist as AI/ML; features themselves were previously cleared, K212333 added the AI/ML marketing claim), K241582 (introduces four new deep-learning cardiac features with quantitative validation: Auto Plane Detection view recognition 97% avg agreement, Quick Strain, Auto LVOT, Auto AoV Doppler auto-trace), and K250328 (UltraExtend NX offline workstation carrying Auto EF/2D WMT Full-assist unchanged from K223017). K252074's only AI feature is an abdominal DL image filter (3-HI). K233195 and K253597 never use AI/ML language; K233195's LAA Analysis is cardiac but not described as AI, and K253597 is a platform migration that names no AI feature. Note that the reference device K223017 (Aplio i-series V7.0, cleared 2023-03-31), which K250328 identifies as the original clearance of the AI/ML Full-assist performance testing, and predicate K242808 (V8.5) are not in this group and may deserve separate triage. WebSearch for Canon 'LAA Analysis' AI returned no source describing that feature as AI/ML (results concerned CT-based LAA deep learning and Canon Echo Fusion, e.g. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9068333/), so the K233195 decision rests on the FDA text alone. Page numbers refer to the '===== PAGE n =====' markers in the extracted text files.
